rules.statement: Don't report a possible CS8603 or nullable warning when a `string?` is returned as non-null after `Assert.False(string.IsNullOrEmpty(x))` or `Assert.True(!string.IsNullOrEmpty(x))` in xUnit test code, and don't ask for a different assertion there.
rules.why: xUnit's `Assert.False` carries `[DoesNotReturnIf(true)]`, so the `[NotNullWhen(false)]` state of `string.IsNullOrEmpty` reaches the return and the build stays clean with warnings as errors.
rules.check: Before raising a nullable-flow finding after an xUnit assertion, check whether the assertion method has a `DoesNotReturnIf` annotation and the checked method has `NotNullWhen`. If both are there, the compiler already proves non-null and there is nothing to report.

rules.statement: When a test class passes the same string literal, such as a route or endpoint path, at several call sites, declare it once as a private const and use the const at each site.
rules.why: If the value changes, a repeated literal has to be updated by hand at every call site.
rules.check: Look for an identical string literal or interpolated constant that appears at several call sites in one class, and suggest a named private const.

rules.statement: Don't suggest making a `CancellationToken` parameter optional (`= default`) to stop call sites passing `CancellationToken.None`. Async methods take the token as a required parameter, and root call sites with no token, including xUnit test methods that get none, pass `CancellationToken.None` explicitly.
rules.why: A required token means a call added inside a cancellable flow can't silently drop cancellation, so explicit `CancellationToken.None` at root call sites is intended, not noise.
rules.check: Before flagging repeated `CancellationToken.None` arguments or a required token parameter, check whether the caller is a root call site with no token in hand, such as a test method or an entry point. If it is, don't report it.
